function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick snapshot of some of the most widely‑publicized festivals happening in the United States in the coming months.  (All dates are for the 2024 edition unless otherwise noted.)  

| Festival | Dates | Location | Genre / Highlights | Ticket Info |
|----------|-------|----------|--------------------|-------------|
| **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | **April 12–14, 2024** | Indio, California | Multi‑genre, art installations, celebrity‑heavy lineup | Tickets start at $395 (early‑bird) – buy at [coachella.com](https://www.coachella.com) |
| **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 27–30, 2024** | Manchester, Tennessee | Rock, hip‑hop, electronic, comedy, food trucks | General admission $295 (early‑bird) – buy at [bonnaroo.com](https://www.bonnaroo.com) |
| **Lollapalooza Chicago** | **August 2–5, 2024** | Chicago, Illinois | Alternative, indie, hip‑hop, pop | General admission $200 (early‑bird) – buy at [lollapalooza.com](https://www.lollapalooza.com) |
| **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | **September 7–9, 2024** | New Orleans, Louisiana | Jazz, blues, world music, Cajun | General admission $125 (early‑bird) – buy at [nojazzfest.com](https://www.nojazzfest.com) |
| **South by Southwest (SXSW)** | **March 8–17, 2024** | Austin, Texas | Film, music, interactive tech | General admission $250 (early‑bird) – buy at [sxsw.com](https://www.sxsw.com) |

### How to Find the “Next” Festival

If you’re looking for the very next festival that’s happening right now (i.e., the one that starts in the next few days), you’ll want to:

1. **Check the dates above** – the earliest date listed is Coachella (April 12).  
2. **Look for smaller, local events** – many cities host week‑long festivals (e.g., food & wine, street fairs) that may start sooner.  
3. **Use a calendar or event‑search site** – sites like Eventbrite, Songkick, or local tourism boards often list upcoming festivals by date.

> **Tip:** Ticket prices and availability can change quickly, so it’s best to book early if you’re interested in a particular festival.

---

#### Quick FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| *Is Coachella the next big festival?* | Yes, it’s the first major U.S. festival of 2024, starting on April 12. |
| *What if I’m only interested in a specific genre?* | Look at the “Genre / Highlights” column – e.g., Bonnaroo is great for rock & electronic, while SXSW covers film & tech. |
| *Where can I buy tickets?* | All tickets are sold through the official festival websites linked in the table. |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more details on any particular festival, or if you’re looking for something more niche (e.g., a food festival, a literary festival, etc.).
